text:
maria: Heads-up — ran the full multilingual eval for veridian-v2 (quant Q4) this morning and hit two weird locale-specific regressions: JA vertical/linewrap mistranslation and AR bracket mirroring flips. numbers look notable: en->ja BLEU 28.3 -> 22.1, chrF 0.62 -> 0.57. en->ar BLEU -1.8 relative. Anyone seen something similar after the last quant kernel update?

jon: ouch. can you paste minimal repro/examples?

maria: quick paste below — these are from the staged eval set (multilang-sanity-v2). same prompts run on baseline (float) vs q4.

maria: SRC (ja, vertical subtitles): 
> 『行ってらっしゃい』と母は背中を押した。
REF: "Take care," she said, pushing him out the door.
BASELINE OUT: "Take care," his mother said as she pushed him out the door.
Q4 OUT: "Take care," his mother said as she pushed him out the door ]

maria: note the stray closing bracket at end — we see this across ~120 ja examples, always with vertical/subtitle-like lines and punctuation near zenkaku-halfwidth boundaries. token counts differ: baseline tokens: 14, q4 tokens: 12 for the same sentence (seems like subtoken merges).

maria: another AR example: SRC (ar, RTL): 
> (هل ستأتي؟)
REF: "Will you come?"
BASELINE OUT: "Will you come?"
Q4 OUT: ")Will you come?("  <-- parens reversed orientation relative to surrounding text

wei: interesting — bracket flipping usually stems from bidi/rendering, but output ordering is different here (not just display). could be detokenization/sign handling in the postproc step after quant kernels prune rare subtokens. did you compare token ids?

maria: yes, quick diff of token ids for the ja example: 
BASELINE_IDS: [101, 2034, 8803, 77, 1203, 900]
Q4_IDS: [101, 2034, 8803, 900]  <-- missing two tokens in middle (token merger)

haruto: that smells like a tokenizer normalization or merge table change. last week we rolled a small change to the byte-level merge heuristic to reduce vocab size for q4 path. maybe it accidentally collapsed halfwidth punctuation into neighbor glyphs for CJK contexts.

jon: can we quickly rule out postproc? i.e., does the raw model decode tokens in the right order before detok?

maria: yes — raw decoded token sequence (pre-detok) for the AR sample is: [LPAREN, text, RPAREN] in baseline but [RPAREN, text, LPAREN] in q4. so ordering changed before detok. not just display.

eval-bot: nightly-multilang-run finished; metadata: run_id=2026-03-21_01, samples=12k, flagged=132, top-flags=['ja-vertical-punct','ar-bracket-bidi','zh-furigana-merge']

wei: plan suggestion: 1) bisect quant kernel changes (q4 host kernels) to find which commit introduced the merge. 2) run token-level diff across a small failing subset to see which merges produce the token-id shifts. 3) run float model with q4 tokenizer/merge table to isolate tokenizer vs model quant path.

haruto: I'll take step 3 — run baseline float weights but point at q4's tokenizer/merge table. if outputs are already flipped then it's tokenizer. also will check our merge rules for 'halfwidth vs fullwidth punctuation' and ZWJ/ZWSP handling (we had a tweak for emoji joiners recently).

liam: i'll hold the veridian-v2 canary on Dedicated. don't want customer traffic hitting a model with bracket flips. set rollout to paused. :thumbsup:

maria: assigning bisect to wei — we need a quick commit range. suspect range: gpu-kernels/quant-opt from 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-14.

wei: ack — starting bisection now. will report in this thread. ETA 2-4 hours depending on repro speed.

jon: couple of quick debug tips: run `--tokenize-only` to print token boundaries and `--render-bidi` to visualize embedding order. example commands: 
```
python tools/eval_slice.py --model veridian-v2 --quant q4 --slice ja-vertical --tokenize-only > ja.tokens
python tools/eval_slice.py --model veridian-float --tokenizer q4table --slice ar-bracket --render-bidi > ar.render
```

maria: adding a small failing subset to the ticket: 15 ja vertical subtitle examples, 10 ar bracket examples, 8 zh-furigana edgecases. I'll open GH issue with samples + raw token ids.

haruto: if tokenizer is root cause, fix options: revert the merge heuristic, patch to explicitly preserve punctuation tokens in CJK context, or add a locale-aware detokenizer pass for vertical text. reverting heuristics likely simplest short-term.

wei: bisection update: narrowed to commit 5a2f3c -> 8b9d11a (quant merge table generator). reproducing locally now with smaller sample.

maria: great — ping when you have the commit. if it's generator bug we should also run all our baseline multilingual smoke sets (esp srt/subtitle and rtl punctuation) before we flip canary back on.

liam: agreed. also schedule a short postmortem with eng-ml + eng-runtime to coordinate kernel+tokenizer release process.

maria: thanks all. tagging @haruto @wei @liam. i'll attach the sample set to the GH issue once created.

wei: update 45m: repro confirms 6c7aab9 in generator drops U+3001 and merges neighbor into previous token in certain contexts — rolling a patch now to skip punctuation merges when prev char is CJK. will land as hotfix and rerun flagged evals.

maria: excellent. will rerun the nightly slice once patch lands.

eval-bot: 4732103490: rerun-complete for hotfix-6c7aab9; flagged reduced: 132 -> 3 (all now non-blocking).

maria: closing loop — hotfix fixed the majority of cases. leaving GH issue open for a follow-up to add targeted unit tests (vertical subtitle, bidi brackets) and extend our quant-onboard smoke matrix. :rocket:
